slide_text: Classes & Objects — Inventing the Model API So far your programs kept data (lists, dicts) and behavior (functions) in separate boxes, and you passed one to the other by hand. A class glues them together: an object carries its own data and the functions that work on it. Why should a machine-learning book care? Because a trained model is an object — some learned numbers plus a function that uses them. By the end of this chapter you will have invented the / pattern that scikit-learn, Keras, and PyTorch all use, hand-built a decision tree out of objects, and saved a model to a file. fragments.text: Answer: B. Inheritance lets you write shared code once in the parent class. The child classes get it for free and only need to add their own unique behavior.

Quick Check — Classes vs. Dicts You built a decision tree using , , and classes. Could you have represented the same tree using nested dictionaries instead? What would you lose? A. Dictionaries cannot be nested, so it is impossible B. It would work, but you would lose the ability to call methods like directly on the tree — you would need separate functions that know the dict structure C. Dictionaries are faster, so you would actually gain performance D. You would lose nothing — classes and dicts are interchangeable

fragments.text: Answer: B. Dicts can be nested, but they carry only data. With classes, the object itself knows how to a question. With dicts you would need a separate function that walks the nested structure manually.

slide_text: Part 6: Saving Objects to Files Your program built a useful tree — then it exits, and the tree is gone. A model you cannot save is a model you must retrain every time. Let's fix that by saving it to a file. JSON files can hold dicts, lists, numbers, strings and booleans — but not your custom objects. So the plan is: object → dict → JSON file , and back again.

Aside — Python's module can serialize almost any object in one line (), no needed. So why bother? A pickle file is Python-only, unreadable by humans, and unsafe to load from untrusted sources. Your JSON file is none of those things. Real ML tooling makes the same trade-off: scikit-learn models ship as pickles (via ), while model configs travel as JSON or YAML.
